growth_explanation.mechanism: WhiteHawk is a natural gas mineral and royalty aggregator (non-operated interests in the Marcellus and Haynesville Shales) that has grown primarily through acquisition (PHX Minerals, closed 2025-06-23; Three Rivers Royalty). Pro forma FY2025 revenue of $89.2 million (giving full-year effect to both acquisitions) versus $9.5 million historical FY2024 shows the scale of inorganic growth; the mechanism has not been separated into organic (price/volume on existing acreage) versus acquisition-driven growth, and no forward acquisition pipeline or reinvestment runway has been disclosed.
growth_explanation.stress: [HUMAN REVIEW] Growth has been driven by two disclosed acquisitions rather than organic production growth on a constant asset base; a stress test needs the reserve decline curve (not yet modeled) to separate a maintenance case (existing PDP decline) from a growth case (further acquisitions, which are not committed capital).

additive_components.evidence: Pro forma Cash Available for Distribution of $36.317m for FY2025 and $9.959m for Q1 2026, from the 424B4 summary financial data. CAFD is defined and reconciled after cash interest expense, cash taxes and cash preferred dividends, so it is an equity-level cash flow and net debt and the mezzanine preferred are deliberately not subtracted again. assumptions.label: Sustainable annual CAFD at OpCo
assumptions.rationale: Q1 2026 pro forma CAFD annualises to $39.8m against $36.3m for pro forma FY2025, so the disclosed run-rate is rising. One quarter is not a year for a commodity royalty, so the base takes the midpoint rather than the latest quarter.

assumptions.label: Company's common economic interest in WhiteHawk OpCo
assumptions.rationale: 86.0% today. The Earnout Amount is 25% of the $130.0m Internalization Price, payable in OpCo Interests and matching Class B if Adjusted EBITDA targets are met; at the $26.00 IPO price that is 1,250,000 units, cutting the Company's interest to 82.1%. Given CAFD is already growing, low and base assume the targets are met and the dilution occurs; only the high case keeps 86.0%.

assumptions.label: Required return on a non-operated gas royalty
assumptions.rationale: No capex and no operating cost, but full commodity exposure, a single-basin pair, a first-year public company with a restated FY2025 and identified material weaknesses, and no declared dividend policy. The low value case carries the high discount rate.

assumptions.label: Net annual change in attributable CAFD
assumptions.rationale: Mineral and royalty interests deplete as wells decline, which sets the low case. But CAFD is struck before acquisition spend, and the stated strategy is to reinvest cash beyond the dividend into more royalties -- royalty revenue ran $12.702m in FY2024, $50.075m in FY2025 and annualises to $102.5m off Q1 2026. Capitalising that as a pure decline would charge depletion while crediting nothing for reinvestment, the mirror of the 'growth without its capital cost' error, so the high case carries modest positive growth. This band is the single largest unverified judgment here and is what the reserve model in the falsifier would replace. For reference, the $26.16 market price implies a ~5.0% cap rate, i.e. roughly +5% perpetual growth at a 10% required return -- above even this high case, so the gap to market is a growth disagreement, not an arithmetic one.

component_valuation_results.partition_note: WhiteHawk Minerals Corp. holds 22,996,579 OpCo Interests (86.0% of common economic interest); Continuing Equity Owners hold 3,750,000 (14.0%), exchangeable 1:1 into Class A. Class B carries votes and no economic rights, so it is not a claim on value and is excluded from the map. The Company owns all Series B preferred units of OpCo, mirroring its own Series B preferred stock, so that leg is intra-group and nets to zero. Note the prospectus also states IPO purchasers hold 24.8% of OpCo indirectly; 33.5% of the Company x 86.0% is 28.8%, so that figure does not tie. The explicit interest counts are used here and the discrepancy is flagged for human review rather than reconciled by assumption.
